text.tspan: Two scale-up topologies: NVL72 switches every GPU to every other in one hop;
a TPU pod wires neighbours in a torus and re-routes cubes optically

g.text: A · NVIDIA NVL72 rack: switched all-to-all
B · Google TPU pod: 3D torus + optical switches

text.tspan: Every GPU has a link to every switch chip (18 on GB200, 36 on Vera Rubin),
so any GPU reaches any other through exactly one switch hop.
Uniform bandwidth: 1.8 TB/s (NVLink 5) or 3.0 TB/s (NVLink 6) per GPU.
Limit: copper reach caps the domain at about one rack (72; 144 with Kyber).
Optical fibre from each cube face
(inside a cube: short copper ICI links to 6 neighbours)
Each chip talks directly only to its 6 torus neighbours (1.2 TB/s on Ironwood).
OCSes close the torus across cubes and swap out failed cubes; they do not
switch packets, so a far chip is many hops away. Huge domain, cheap per chip,
but bandwidth to a distant chip is shared along the path.
